source_text:
Πέρας γοῦν ἰδόντες οἱ ἄνομοι μὴ δυνάμενον αὐτοῦ τὸ σῶμα ὑπὸ τοῦ πυρὸς δαπανηθῆναι, ἐκέλευσαν προσελθόντα αὐτῷ κομφέκτορα παραβῦσαι ξιφίδιον. καὶ τοῦτο ποιήσαντος, ἐξῆλθεν περιστερὰ καὶ πλῆθος αἵματος, ὥστε κατασβέσαι τὸ πῦρ καὶ θαυμάσαι πάντα τὸν ὄχλον, εἰ τοσαύτη τις διαφορὰ μεταξὺ τῶν τε ἀπίστων καὶ τῶν ἐκλεκτῶν:
ὧν εἷς καὶ οὗτος γεγόνει ὁ θαυμασιώτατος μάρτυς Πολύκαρπος, ἐν τοῖς καθ̓ ἡμᾶς χρόνοις διδάσκαλος ἀποστολικὸς καὶ προφητικὸς γενόμενος, ἐπίσκοπος τῆς ἐν Σμύρνῃ καθολικῆς ἐκκλησίας. πᾶν γὰρ ῥῆμα, ὃ ἀφῆκεν ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ. καὶ ἐτελειώθη καὶ τελειωθήσεται.
orientation: The fire has failed to consume Polycarp's body, and the lawless men now order a confector to stab him.
pass_a_gloss: So when the lawless men saw that his body could not be consumed by the fire, they ordered a confector to come up to him and thrust in a dagger. And when he did this, a dove came out and a great quantity of blood, so that the fire was quenched and the whole crowd marveled, whether there is so great a difference between the unbelievers and the elect: of whom this one also had become one, the most wonderful martyr Polycarp, having become in our times an apostolic and prophetic teacher, bishop of the catholic church in Smyrna. For every word that he sent forth from his mouth both was fulfilled and will be fulfilled.

choices.why: A technical Latin loanword for the arena official who dispatches a victim; keeping it preserves the Roman institutional setting.
The verb παραβύω means to push or stuff in, emphasizing the forceful insertion; dagger is the standard rendering of ξιφίδιον.
The verb ἐξῆλθεν is simple and literal; the dove is a miraculous sign, so the plain wording preserves the wonder.
πλῆθος means a large amount or multitude; rendering it as great quantity keeps the literal force.

choices.english: of whom this one also had become one
choices.why: The relative clause is awkward in Greek; keeping the literal structure preserves the emphasis that Polycarp belonged to the elect.
rejected: one of whom this man also had become
to which number this man also belonged

choices.english: both was fulfilled and will be fulfilled
choices.why: The verb τελειόω here means to bring to completion or fulfillment; the perfect and future tenses show the enduring authority of Polycarp's words.
rejected: was perfected and will be perfected
was accomplished and will be accomplished

pass_b_english: When the lawless men saw that his body could not be consumed by the fire, they ordered a confector to go up to him and thrust in a dagger. When he did this, a dove came out, along with a great quantity of blood, so that it quenched the fire and made the whole crowd marvel that there was such a great difference between the unbelievers and the elect.

One of the elect was this man, the most wonderful martyr Polycarp, who in our own times was an apostolic and prophetic teacher, bishop of the catholic church in Smyrna. For every word that came from his mouth both was fulfilled and will be fulfilled.

last_rejected.why: The Greek term refers to a gladiator or executioner (from Latin confector), not a pastry maker.
last_rejected.fix: they ordered a gladiator to go up to him and thrust in a dagger.
last_rejected.ruling: English 'confector' is correct Latin loanword transliteration; means executioner/gladiator, not pastry maker. No error.

problems.quote: a confector to go up to him and thrust in a dagger
problems.why: “Confector” likely mistranslates a term for the executioner.

problems.quote: the church of Smyrna wrote this letter
problems.why: Sender identified as 'church of Smyrna' then 'church of God that sojourns in Smyrna'; reader may miss identity.

variants.text: The church of God that sojourns in Smyrna
bishop of the catholic church in Smyrna

problems.quote: a dove came out, along with a great quantity of blood, so that it quenched the fire
problems.why: Physical impossibility as stated; dove and blood from dagger wound unclear.
problems.fix: Note symbolic/miraculous intent; possibly 'dove' is later interpolation.

edits.old: a confector to go up to him and thrust in a dagger
edits.new: an executioner to go up to him and thrust in a dagger

fixed: The glossary problem about the sender is not present in this section; no edit needed.
The dove and blood are rendered as the source states; the English already conveys the miraculous event as written.

polish.changed: Replaced the obscure Latin loanword 'confector' with 'executioner', clarified the sequence of the dove and blood, and kept the paragraph break where the thought turns from the crowd's marvel to Polycarp's identity.
